user.title: Which meter sensors?
user.description: Choose the cumulative energy sensors for the energy you buy from the grid and, if you have them, the energy you send back and a controlled load register. A cost sensor is created for each.

data_description.import_entity: Must measure energy bought from the grid (not whole-house consumption). Wh, kWh and MWh sensors work.
data_description.export_entity: Energy sent to the grid. Leave empty if you have no solar.
data_description.controlled_load_entity: Energy on a separately metered controlled load circuit, if your bill has controlled load lines.

bill.title: How does your bill print prices?
bill.description: Look at the usage and supply charge lines on your electricity bill.

data_description.rates_include_gst: Most Australian bills show GST-inclusive prices. Untick if yours are GST-exclusive and 10% is added. Feed-in is never given GST.
data_description.discount_percent: A guaranteed discount percentage, if your plan has one. Leave at 0 if the prices you enter already have it applied.
data_description.discount_scope: Most plans discount usage only; some also discount the daily supply charge. Check the discount line on your bill.
data_description.window_time: Most Victorian, NSW and SA plans use the clock on the wall, so windows move with daylight saving. Some plans (for example in Tasmania and the ACT) define windows in standard time, so they appear an hour later on the clock during daylight saving. Your plan's fact sheet will say.
data_description.holiday_state: Choose your state or territory if your plan treats public holidays differently from normal days.
data_description.holidays_as: Some plans have no peak rates on public holidays, treating them like a weekend. Others treat them as normal days.

charges.title: Daily charges
charges.description: Enter these exactly as printed on your bill. The supply charge is a fixed amount for each day. It is added to the Import cost sensor, so it is included in the cost the Energy dashboard shows for your grid import.

data.extra_daily: Other fixed daily charge or credit ({day_unit})

data_description.extra_daily: For example a daily membership fee, or a daily credit entered as a negative number. Leave at 0 if none.

structure.title: How are your usage rates structured?
structure.description: Pick the closest match. Typical time windows are filled in for you and you only type in the prices from your bill; you can change any window. Choose a step structure if your price changes after a number of kWh per day, or Custom to build your own.

periods.title: Usage rates
periods.description:
{progress}.

Enter the usage price for each time window on your bill.

Times are local clock time. An end time earlier than the start runs past midnight, and the same start and end means all day. Windows must cover every minute of every day exactly once.

Added so far:
{periods}

data.name: Name
data.add_another: Add another rate after this one
data.start_over: Discard the rates above and start again

data_description.step_kwh: Leave empty unless the price changes after a number of kWh. Examples: the first 11 kWh per day at one price and the rest at another (step rates); a free window that is only free up to a daily cap; feed-in paid at a higher rate for the first kWh exported each day.
data_description.rate_after: Only needed when you fill in an allowance.

feed_in_structure.title: How is your solar feed-in paid?
feed_in_structure.description: Choose a single flat rate, a higher rate for the first kWh exported each day (tiered), or different rates at different times of day.

feed_in_periods.title: Feed-in rates
feed_in_periods.description:
{progress}.

Enter what you are paid per kWh exported. For a tiered feed-in, put the higher rate in Price and the daily kWh it applies to in Allowance, then the standard rate in Price after the allowance. Negative prices are allowed.

Times are local clock time. An end time earlier than the start runs past midnight, and the same start and end means all day. Windows must cover every minute of every day exactly once.

data_description.rate_after: Only needed when you fill in an allowance.

cl_structure.title: Controlled load rates
cl_structure.description: Controlled load (for example hot water on its own meter register) usually has one price all day.

extras.title: Anything else on your bill?
extras.description: Optional. Skip this if neither applies to your plan.

data.demand_enabled: My plan has a demand charge
data.step_anchor: Allowance cycle starts on (only if longer than 1 day)

data_description.demand_enabled: A charge based on your highest half-hour demand (kW) during a peak window.
data_description.step_reset_days: 1 for allowances that reset daily (most common). Use your billing period length for allowances such as 'first 1,000 kWh per quarter'.
data_description.step_anchor: A date when one of your allowance periods began.

demand.title: Demand charge
demand.description: The charge is your highest 30 minute average demand in kW inside the window, in a calendar month, times the price. Use the same units as your bill.

error.gap: Some part of the week has no rate. Add another rate to fill the gap.
error.overlap: Two rates overlap. Tick 'Discard the rates above' to start again.
error.step_needs_rate: Enter the price that applies after the allowance.
